lesson.menu_desc: Telling a short story from a trip or from work with the past continuous + past simple: I was waiting at the gate when... -- 31 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 21 -- Telling Stories: Anecdotes
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Aline Sberci | Lesson 21 -- Telling Stories: Anecdotes
lesson.grammar_point: past continuous + past simple (was/were + -ing ... when ... / while ...)

listenings.text: Okay, here is my embarrassing story. Last year, I was presenting our new project to the directors. Everything was going well. I was showing the first chart when suddenly the fire alarm started. Everybody left the building, and we waited outside for twenty minutes. It was raining, and we were all standing in the parking lot. Meanwhile, my laptop was still in the meeting room with my presentation open. When we went back in, I realized that the directors were reading my slides without me. Luckily, they liked the project, and they approved it the same day. So now, every time I present, I check where the exit is.

Welcome to Travel Stories. My name is Daniel, and today I have a short anecdote from my trip to Switzerland. I was traveling by train from Zurich to Basel. The trip is only one hour, so I was not worried. I was reading a book while the train was moving, and the view was beautiful. Then I started to feel tired, and I closed my eyes for a minute. When I opened them, the train was not moving, and the station was very quiet. Unfortunately, I was not in Basel. I was in a small town near the French border. I was scared for a moment, but a woman at the station helped me, and I took the next train back. I arrived two hours late, but I had a great story to tell.

extra_audio.text: Last spring, Aline was flying to Basel for a project meeting. She was waiting at the gate when she suddenly noticed that her phone was dead. While she was looking for a charger, they changed the gate. Luckily, a kind man told her about the new gate. In the end, she got on the plane, and now it is her favorite anecdote.

items.situation: Your colleague asks: What were you doing at eight o'clock last night? Answer with was + -ing.
Tell what happened: you were driving to work. Your boss called you.
Tell what happened: you were waiting at the gate. The airline changed the gate.
Two things at the same time: you were writing a report. Your team was having lunch.
Your friend says: I was walking in the park when I saw a famous actor. React and ask a question.
